scope: Independent reproduction of baseline LLVM object-cache publication failure; neither CP22 nor CP26 introduced this code.

finding.mechanism: The store closure includes create_new.open, and its error cleanup removes the temporary path for every Err, even AlreadyExists before ownership.
finding.observable_effect: Post-publication object-cache commit removes a successfully published executable whose path equals objects-v1/<namespace>/.pending-<compiler PID>-0. CLI still reports Success and Verify=1, with one object-cache write_failure.
finding.minimal_fix: Acquire/create the temporary file before installing cleanup or ensure cleanup is conditioned on successful acquisition. Disarm only after successful rename.
required_controls: Preexisting temporary-path sentinel and native executable survive AlreadyExists unchanged.
Owned temporary files are cleaned on post-create I/O/rename failure; existing final entry survives.
Success still yields a reusable cache entry and fresh request Verify.

reproduction.mechanism: object_cache::store cleanup runs for every error, including create_new AlreadyExists before ownership. Post-publication cache commit deletes the requested native output.

summary_extraction_note: The original reproduction result used report.get(object_cache) at the top level and emitted null for that convenience field. The authoritative original raw report carries native_codegen.object_cache; this review extracts and checks the real nested status without rewriting the original log. Native output deletion and Success/Verify assertions were unaffected.
limits: Frozen baseline binary hash independently rechecked; no independent release rebuild.
Deliberate deterministic collision in reviewer-created private directory, no hostile writer modeled.
Current CP26 write scope is parse cache only; separate authorized correction required.
